title: Cascade Health - regional fence & secure endpoint pilot scoping
summary: Initial POC scoping to define success criteria and network topology for a private-network, region-locked inference pilot. Main decisions: start with VPC peering in us-east-1, test PrivateLink fallback for egress-restricted environments, run bench against 6 concurrent clients simulating 40 QPS total, 3-week bench + 1-week analysis window.
topics: egress constraints and egress firewall rules
benchmarks: latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost per 1k tokens
next_steps: Emily to share network diagram, bench script, and pricing worksheet by 2027-03-06
Customer to confirm VPC CIDR ranges and peering approval by 2027-03-08
Schedule bench window: week of 2027-03-15 (3 business days) - Redwood/Customer to confirm exact days
action_items: Emily Carter - send network diagram, sample terraform and bench harness link - due 2027-03-06
Jordan Lin - prepare bench harness with 3 workload shapes (chat, completions, embeddings) and test tokens - due 2027-03-10
Miguel Santos - confirm security controls and provide egress ACL and expected NAT behavior - due 2027-03-08
Lena Park - share SOC2 scope and KMS integration requirements - due 2027-03-09
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-04 14:00 UTC
Duration: 00:52:00
Attendees: Emily Carter (Redwood AE); Jordan Lin (Redwood SE); Ravi Menon (Redwood Solutions Eng); Dr. Priya Rao (Cascade CTO); Miguel Santos (Infra Lead); Lena Park (Security); Tom Becker (Product)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to scope a private-network POC for inference with region lock and strict egress. Discussed peering vs privatelink, bench sizing, success metrics, timeline and next steps.

[00:00:10] Emily: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick intros then we'll go through goals for the pilot. real quick if you could say name and role.
[00:00:21] Dr. Priya Rao: Priya, CTO at Cascade, we run a HIPAA adjacent platform, need residency in us-east-1 and want to avoid any cross-region egress.
[00:00:29] Miguel: Miguel, infra, I manage our VPCs and edge NATs, we have strict egress gateway and firewall.
[00:00:35] Emily: Great, Jordan?
[00:00:37] Jordan: Jordan Lin, SE from Redwood, I will own the bench and performance side.
[00:00:40] Tom: Tom product, interested in latency and cost delta.
[00:00:44] Lena: Lena security, SOC 2, KMS, audit logs are big for us.

[00:01:05] Emily: Ok goals: define topology - VPC peering versus PrivateLink, confirm region lock, bench sizing and success criteria, timeline. We usually do a 3-week bench and 1-week analysis for this size of customer. Thoughts?
[00:01:22] Dr. Priya Rao: We prefer peering if possible, but our security posture requires all egress to go through an approved gateway and logs kept. Also, for compliance we need key control - so K M S integration or HSM.
[00:01:36] Miguel: yeah peering adds extra routes but simpler for our NAT. PrivateLink would be good if we can't peer because of org boundaries, but we worry about data egress paths still, need to see how egress to S3 or metrics endpoints is handled.
[00:01:50] Jordan: Helpful, thanks. From Redwood's side we can support both. Peering gives fewer hops and generally lower p99 latencies because you stay inside the cloud fabric. PrivateLink gives stronger isolation per endpoint and avoids route-table changes, but egress behavior depends on interface endpoints and our egress policy.
[00:02:10] Tom: Do you have any measured deltas? Like ballpark p95 differences?
[00:02:14] Jordan: Ballpark: peering often shows p95 ~ 20-40ms lower for small seq lengths, p99 improvement too but depends on region and instance types. Not exact but we will run an apples-to-apples bench.
[00:02:26] Dr. Priya Rao: ok, good. On residency: we must ensure no requests go to other regions and all data-at-rest stays in us-east-1. Also retention rules - logs for 365 days.
[00:02:40] Lena: and audit trails for key operations. KMS wrapping required, keys must be customer-managed.

[00:03:05] Emily: Noted. Bench plan: Jordan, propose 3 workload shapes. Chat (multi-turn) at 6 concurrent users simulating 20 QPS, Completions (single shot) 10 concurrent at 15 QPS, and Embeddings batch workload 4 workers at 5 QPS. Combined target approx 40 QPS sustained. Does that align with your expected workload?
[00:03:27] Miguel: we typically see bursts up to 60 QPS but sustained at 30-40 so yes that seems right. What about context lengths?
[00:03:33] Jordan: We'll test with 512 tokens context for chat and 128 for completions; embeddings payload sizes ~ 2-4k tokens per batch depending on batch size. We'll send actual bench harness so you can replicate.

[00:03:55] Emily: Success criteria suggestions: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 250ms for completions at target QPS, p99 < 500ms or graceful degradation with fallback; throughput sustained at 40 QPS for 3 business days; cost per 1k tokens under expected bound - we'll define that in pricing worksheet.
[00:04:15] Tom: For product, we also want quality parity—no regressions vs our current model. How do we track quality?
[00:04:20] Jordan: We'll run a small eval set of prompts and check for divergence. Redwood Optimize can run diff checks with thresholds. We'll include those artifacts and tie alerts to regression thresholds.

[00:04:45] Dr. Priya Rao: About private keys, can Redwood integrate with our KMS? We need customer-managed keys, ideally HSM backed.
[00:04:52] Jordan: Yes, we support customer KMS for model keys and storage; there are two modes — envelope encryption with customer KMS or full HSM integration for Private deployment. For Hosted/dedicated we can do envelope KMS and log key usage. We'll put the tech note in the security packet.

[00:05:10] Lena: We also need access controls: RBAC for who can call endpoints and token rotation windows.
[00:05:15] Emily: Redwood Console supports token-scoped grants and can integrate with SAML SSO for team mapping; we'll include docs.

[00:05:30] Miguel: On networking, peering requires routes added to our route tables. Is there a service account or ASG on your side? How much ops work for us?
[00:05:40] Jordan: For peering we ask for VPC ID and CIDR and we'll create a peer on our side and send the peer request. You accept and add route table entries. PrivateLink requires you create an interface endpoint in your subnet and we'll provide the service name. PrivateLink avoids route table changes but needs ENIs and security group rules. We'll provide terraform snippets to simplify.

[00:06:05] Tom: What about egress to telemetry or S3? We can't have any egress that passes through public internet.
[00:06:12] Emily: We can route telemetry to a customer S3 bucket via VPC endpoint or push logs over the peering link; for metrics we can deliver to a private endpoint. We'll document the endpoints and options.

[00:06:28] Dr. Priya Rao: Good. Bench observability — we need traces per token and cost breakdown by route, can you give token-level cost and latency per route?
[00:06:36] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency, and you can break down by model, route, and API key. We'll set up a dashboard for the bench and share read-only links during the pilot.

[00:06:52] Miguel: Any pitfalls customers hit during peering?
[00:06:55] Jordan: Two common issues: route-table conflicts and MTU mismatches if there are vpn overlays. Also if you use egress proxies they sometimes rewrite TLS which breaks HMAC signatures. We'll run a small connectivity test to validate handshake and route.

[00:07:14] Emily: On timelines we propose: week 1 - network setup and security review; week 2 - bench deployment and dry runs; week 3 - full bench window (3 business days) and initial analysis; week 4 - deep analysis and next-step decision. Is that acceptable?
[00:07:29] Dr. Priya Rao: Yes that fits our internal quarterly planning but we need approvals from compliance so maybe add a contingency week.

[00:07:40] Tom: Cost expectations—what's rough for a 3-week pilot?
[00:07:44] Emily: Depends on model size and tokens; we'll share a pricing worksheet. For an initial bench using small models and quantized variants, ballpark could be Xk USD — we'll send exact numbers once we agree workloads.

[00:07:58] Jordan: Also a note: if you require region lock, we'll pin instances and model cache to us-east-1 and disable cross-region fallback. That may reduce capacity options but respects residency.

[00:08:14] Lena: And that pinning—does it affect our SLA or fallbacks?
[00:08:18] Jordan: It does reduce fallback options. We can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model variant within the same region only. If capacity constrained we can enable burst to dedicated reserved capacity which you'd approve during pilot. We'll include a fallback policy in the configuration.

[00:08:36] Miguel: For the bench harness where's it hosted? We prefer to run harness from inside our VPC to hit the private endpoints end-to-end.
[00:08:44] Jordan: We can run the client inside your VPC; we'll provide the harness as a Docker container and terraform for interface endpoints. Alternatively Redwood can run a client from our infra over the peering if you want us to simulate outside-in. Best is to run both to compare.

[00:09:02] Dr. Priya Rao: Ok both sounds good. For data retention during bench — logs containing PII must be redacted or hashed.
[00:09:08] Emily: We'll add a redaction step and can run bench with synthetic data; we recommend synthetic where possible and hashed tokens otherwise.

[00:09:20] Tom: Who signs off on success? Product / infra / security?
[00:09:24] Dr. Priya Rao: All three, plus legal for a procurement go-ahead.

[00:09:35] Emily: Cool. Let's put some concrete numbers down: success criteria list that we'll track.
[00:09:40] Jordan: I'll read them out: 1) sustain 40 QPS across combined workloads for 72h with <5% error rate, 2) completions p95 < 250ms at target QPS, p99 < 500ms or controlled degradation with fallback, 3) no cross-region outbound traffic detected (verified by packet capture and cloudflow logs), 4) KMS key usage logged and customer key never leaves customer control, 5) cost per 1k tokens within agreed threshold.

[00:10:10] Miguel: For networking verification how do you demonstrate 'no cross-region'?
[00:10:14] Jordan: We'll provide connection logs, TCP dumps from the client and server side, and route table confirmation. We'll also use VPC flow logs and our audit logs to show endpoints.

[00:10:25] Lena: For KMS we need rotation policy and proof that Redwood cannot export plaintext keys.
[00:10:30] Emily: We'll share a KMS integration spec and auditor notes for key handling.

[00:10:45] Dr. Priya Rao: Ok good. A few odd questions: do you support token-level throttling by API key? We need to throttle some internal users.
[00:10:52] Jordan: Yes, rate limits by API key and token quota policies; we can preconfigure token budgets per service account.

[00:11:05] Tom: Bench scheduling: prefer 3 consecutive weekdays in the middle of March if possible.
[00:11:10] Emily: Suggested window week of March 15-19; Jordan will propose exact 3 days after we get peering confirmation.

[00:11:20] Miguel: On PEERING detail: we will require an infra ticket for route changes. Do you have an automation to create the accept request?
[00:11:26] Jordan: We create the peer and generate the request; you'll accept and add the route. We'll provide terraform so the change is minimal and auditable.

[00:11:40] Dr. Priya Rao: If PrivateLink is used will there be additional ENI charges?
[00:11:44] Emily: Yes, PrivateLink interface endpoints have per-hour charges and ENI costs. We'll include cost delta in the worksheet. Peering typically cheaper.

[00:11:56] Tom: Any regulatory concerns about logs leaving our account?
[00:12:00] Lena: Logs must remain in our account or an approved S3 bucket in us-east-1.
[00:12:03] Emily: We'll deliver logs to your S3 bucket via VPC endpoint.

[00:12:12] Jordan: Ok I'll outline the bench scenarios now: scenario A - chat 6 users multi-turn, payload 512 tokens, sequence length avg 350; scenario B - completions single shot 128 tokens; scenario C - embeddings batched 256 vectors per batch. We'll provide the harness.

[00:12:35] Miguel: How do you instrument cost per 1k tokens? We need exact breakdown.
[00:12:40] Jordan: The console gives token-level accounting with model id, route (peering vs privatelink), and token type (prompt vs completion). We'll export a CSV for analysis.

[00:12:50] Dr. Priya Rao: Great. For the bench we need to run some long tail tests for p99 — can you extend the run to capture p99 over longer window?
[00:12:57] Jordan: Yes we'll run extended tail sampling and provide p99, p999 samples and error traces.

[00:13:10] Emily: All right, anything else on topology?
[00:13:13] Miguel: MTU note - we operate with jumbo frames across our network overlays, watch out for smaller MTU on interface endpoints.
[00:13:19] Jordan: noted. We'll include MTU checks in the connectivity test script.

[00:13:30] Tom: Customer asks what happens if capacity is constrained during bench - do you auto scale?
[00:13:35] Jordan: For hosted we have autoscaling but cross-region fallback limited by region lock. If autoscale can't keep up we recommend bursted reserved capacity (dedicated) for the bench. We'll propose a short-term reserved capacity option for bench days.

[00:13:48] Dr. Priya Rao: Any contractual change if we enable dedicated reserved capacity?
[00:13:52] Emily: That would be an add-on with a short commit for the bench period; we'll include terms in the pricing worksheet.

[00:14:05] Miguel: For the bench harness, we want to provide a list of internal IPs and security groups that the harness will use.
[00:14:12] Jordan: Good call, we'll supply the client IPs and security group recommendations.

[00:14:25] Emily: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[00:14:28] Emily: Emily will send network diagram, terraform snippets, bench harness link and pricing worksheet by 2027-03-06.
[00:14:35] Emily: Jordan will prepare the bench harness with three workload shapes and the evaluation script by 2027-03-10.
[00:14:41] Emily: Miguel to confirm VPC CIDRs and approve peering or request PrivateLink by 2027-03-08.
[00:14:46] Emily: Lena to share SOC2 scope and KMS requirements by 2027-03-09.
[00:14:50] Tom: we'll review and get back with schedule the same week.

[00:15:05] Dr. Priya Rao: Thanks all. Quick note - can Redwood provide a one-page security sprint doc for our review?
[00:15:12] Emily: Yes will include a condensed security brief with the packet.

[00:15:20] (crosstalk)
[00:15:30] Jordan: I'll also put together a connectivity checklist: VPC IDs, subnets, route tables, SG rules, ENI configuration for PrivateLink, MTU notes.

[00:15:40] Emily: Great. Any blockers?
[00:15:44] Miguel: dependency on our change control for peering acceptance - might push bench by a few days but we should be ok.
[00:15:52] Dr. Priya Rao: we want to keep the bench in-east-1 only.

[00:16:00] Emily: noted. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.

(remaining time used for side conversations and tribal knowledge sharing, approx 36 minutes — short check-ins on internal process that Fireflies clipped)

[00:52:00] Meeting ended
